report.clinical_summary: The patient presents with persistent fatigue (several months) and recent constant headaches (last couple of weeks). They have an HIV diagnosis and are on Triumeq for 3 years. They've tried self-care strategies (breaks, exercise, eating well) but nothing has helped. They've noticed that when they miss doses or take 'drug holidays,' symptoms go away temporarily. They haven't discussed these symptoms with their HIV doctor yet. They feel emotionally affected - experiencing both anxiety and constant worry. They don't have a clear understanding of what's causing their symptoms and feel mostly out of control.

consequences.reasoning: The patient has lost major roles - struggling to get through workdays, skipping social events with friends, collapsing on the couch after dinner. They can barely manage their usual routine. This fits the 8 scale where a major role is lost or substantially reduced.
